<thought>To determine the number of aromatic carbons, I will examine the 13C NMR spectrum. Aromatic carbons typically appear between ~110 ppm and ~160 ppm. The spectrum shows peaks at 168.60 ppm, 143.85 ppm, and 130.30 ppm in that region. The 168.60 ppm peak is likely a carbonyl carbon, not aromatic. The remaining two peaks (143.85 ppm and 130.30 ppm) fall within the aromatic range, indicating two distinct aromatic carbon environments. Therefore, the molecule contains **2 aromatic carbons**.</thought>
<final_answer>2</final_answer>
